jobs.title: Business Operations
jobs.description:
Exa is an applied AI lab building a search engine unlike the world has ever seen. We build massive-scale infra to crawl the entire web, train state-of-the-art embedding models to process it, and design super high performant vector databases to retrieve over it. We now power search for Cursor, Cognition, HubSpot, and over 400,000 developers and have raised $350m from Lightspeed, Benchmark, and a16z.

 

Our ultimate goal is to build perfect search over all the world's information, far beyond Google. If you want to build massive-scale ML systems that will define the way the new AI world consumes information, this is the place for you.



Business Operations at Exa

Exa is growing faster than the systems that run it. This is a generalist role for someone early in their career who wants real ownership of how a company operates — you'll work across finance, ops, and G&A, building the machinery that lets a small, dense team run a company serving 400,000+ developers.

You'll go wherever the company is breaking, scope the problem, build the fix, and hand it off. And you'll do it AI-natively — we expect the person in this seat to replace manual work with agents and internal tooling rather than absorb it as headcount. How we operate is part of our advantage, not back-office overhead.

You'll work directly with the founders and every function lead here. Most of what you'll own doesn't exist yet — you'll be the one who builds it.

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Put AI to work inside Exa — Find work that people are doing and AI should be. Build AI workflows and internal tooling that eliminate manual steps across finance and ops, and become the person the team comes to for what's worth automating and how.

 - Support FinOps and cost discipline — Help us understand and control what we spend. Track infrastructure and vendor costs, pull analysis that shows where the money is going, flag what looks off, and support the work to bring it down.

 - Build the systems behind AP and AR — Own the day-to-day mechanics of money moving in and out: vendor onboarding and payments, customer invoicing, billing accuracy, collections follow-up, and expense workflows. Turn the parts that live in someone's inbox into processes that run on their own.

 - Run cross-functional projects end to end — Take on the ambiguous work that doesn't belong to any one team and drive it from scoping to done.

 - Support the people who own the numbers — Partner with finance and leadership on planning inputs, budget-vs-actual tracking, and the analysis behind decisions.

 - Pick up what needs doing — This is an early team. Some of the highest-value work will be things nobody has written down yet.

 
 


WHAT YOU'LL NEED

 - 3-6 years of experience in investment banking, management consulting, accounting, strategic finance, or business operations at a high-growth technology company

 - Genuinely AI-native — you already use LLMs and agents as leverage in your daily work and have built things with them.

 - A builder's instinct for process — when something breaks twice, you redesign it. When a task takes four hours every week, you make it run itself

 - Comfort with data — you can pull your own numbers, work confidently in spreadsheets, and don't need someone else to answer a question for you

 - Extremely high attention to detail — this role touches money moving in and out of the company. Small errors are expensive

 - High ownership and high tolerance for ambiguity — you take things from vague to done without being managed through it, and you're comfortable switching contexts several times a day

 - Clear communication — you can write a crisp update, chase an overdue invoice professionally, and explain a process to someone who has no context

Exa is an equal opportunity employer. We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We’re high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.


About the Role

Reporting directly to co-founder Jeff Wang, the VP Finance will be Exa’s first dedicated finance leader and a key member of the executive leadership team, driving financial strategy, operational rigor, and business insight across the organization. This role requires a strategic thinker with strong leadership capabilities, exceptional financial acumen, and a proven track record in building financial infrastructures to support hyper growth. Equally important is the ability to operate as a true business partner - someone who can translate complex financial data into clear strategic insights, partner closely with GTM and product leadership, and communicate with precision and confidence to the founders, board, and investors. With its Series C just closed and revenue scaling rapidly, Exa needs a leader who brings rigor to both compute-driven unit economics and top-line growth, while building the finance function from 0 to 1.


Responsibilities

Build the Finance Function

 - Establish internal controls, systems, and processes to support scale and audit readiness

 - Bring core accounting and finance operations in-house

 -  Hire and develop a high-caliber finance team from the ground up

Financial Planning & Analysis / Financial Operations:

 - Build and own financial models and forecasting suited to a consumption-based API business

 - Own company-wide budgeting and scenario planning

 - Establish and refine FP&A processes that give leadership real financial visibility and support fast, data-driven decisions

 - Ensure the integrity of financial reporting and compliance with applicable regulations.

Strategic Finance

 - Serve as a key strategic partner to the leadership team on all financial decisions - from pricing and unit economics to capital allocation

 - Partner with GTM on pricing, packaging, and strategic deal-making

 - Partner with Engineering on infrastructure and product decisions that carry unit-economic implications

 - Own capital allocation strategy and treasury

Fundraising & Investor Relations

 - Own investor reporting and board communications

 - Prepare Exa for future financing events - Series D and beyond

Qualifications:

 - Bachelor’s degree in finance, accounting, or a related field

 - 8 - 15 years of finance experience, with meaningful time at a high-growth technology company

 - Strategic finance background: IB, PE, venture capital, or growth-stage operator experience

 - Track record building a finance function at a scaling startup - you’ve seen what great looks like and how to build it

 -  Deep fluency in financial modeling and FP&A for API/consumption-based business models

 - Hands-on experience managing compute costs in an infrastructure, AI, or usage-based business

 - Strong commercial instincts - ability to partner closely with GTM leadership on revenue strategy, pricing, and unit economics

 - Experience leading institutional fundraising

 - Exceptional communicator - concise, direct, and able to distill complex financial data into clear executive and board-level insights

 - Operator mentality: moves fast, builds from scratch, and thrives in ambiguity

 - Low ego, high accountability - a collaborator who earns trust through execution

Location

 - Targeting San Francisco Bay Area as preferred location

jobs.title: Digital Marketing Manager
jobs.description:
About Exa

We raised a $250M Series C to build the search engine for AIs. Led by a16z, with existing investors Benchmark, Lightspeed, and YC doubling down, the round brings Exa's valuation to $2.2 billion. 

Exa is building a search engine for the AI era. Our Search API currently powers Agents, Fortune 500s and AI labs as we transform an industry that hasn't been disrupted since the 90s. We're a largely SF-based team of ~100 from Harvard, MIT, Meta, Google Research, ex-founders & dropouts alike.

We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We're high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.

We are looking for a Digital Marketing Manager to own the channels and surfaces where developers find us and decide to sign up.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This is a full-stack growth role. You own paid acquisition, the website and its conversion path, and the technical mechanics of search and answer-engine visibility. You need to be genuinely hands-on in all of them rather than a manager of agencies.

Developers can be cynical about marketing, allergic to gated content, and they evaluate by trying the product. So the job is less about clever campaigns and more about removing friction: fast load-times, a signup flow that gets someone to their first API success, and spend that goes where developers are.

You will work closely with Technical PMM, who owns the content narrative, while you own the surfaces and channels that distribute it. You'll also work with Marketing Ops, who owns the tech-stack and attribution method, while you own channel performance.

This is an AI-first role at an AI-first company. Creative production, landing page velocity, and reporting should be AI-accelerated so that one person can run three functions.

This role is based in-person at our San Francisco HQ.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN




PAID ACQUISITION

Own paid channels end to end: search, social, developer-native placements (newsletters, podcasts, communities, sponsorships), budget allocation, creative testing, and channel mix. Success is measured by qualified signups and pipeline per dollar, with an honest view of incrementality.




WEBSITE AND CONVERSION

Own the marketing site as a conversion surface: landing pages, page speed, messaging tests, and the path from first visit to signup. Success is measured by conversion rate improvements you can defend and by shipping velocity on new pages.




SEARCH AND ANSWER ENGINE MECHANICS

Own the technical side of organic visibility: site architecture, crawlability, schema and structured data, page performance, and the tooling that monitors it. You can collaborate with Technical PMM to identify and pursue target keywords.




SELF-SERVE FUNNEL GROWTH

Own the top of the self-serve funnel through to activation handoff: signup flow experiments, friction removal, and the instrumentation to see where developers drop. Success is measured by signup-to-first-call conversion.




CHANNEL REPORTING AND EXPERIMENTATION

Own channel-level reporting, the experiment backlog, and the discipline of running tests that produce decisions. Marketing Ops owns the attribution model and the source of truth; you own performance within it and you use the same numbers everyone else does.




AI-FIRST EXECUTION

Design and deploy AI-powered workflows for creative variants, page builds, keyword and audience research, and reporting. If a step runs manually more than twice, you should be itching to automate it.




WHAT THIS ROLE DOES NOT OWN

 - Technical content, benchmarks, and the organic narrative: Technical PMM for Content.

 - Marketing tech stack, data model, and attribution methodology: Marketing Operations is primary, but you can influence of course.

 - Email, nurture, and webinars: that’s Lifecycle Marketing.

 - Events and field programs: Field Marketing and Field Events.

 - Product onboarding beyond the marketing funnel handoff: Product and Engineering.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - Qualified signups grow while keeping CAC in range, and you can show which channels are incremental.

 - New landing pages ship in days.

 - The site is technically clean: fast, crawlable, structured, and monitored.

 - Signup-to-first-API-call conversion improves through experiments you ran.

 - You and Technical PMM operate together on organic.

 - Spend decisions are made weekly from data, and losing channels get cut.




WHO YOU ARE

 - 4+ years in growth, digital, or performance marketing at a B2B technology company, with hands-on ownership of paid budgets, landing pages, and technical SEO. Not agency oversight, hands on keyboard.

 - Deep craft in at least one of the three areas and real working competence in the other two. Tell us which is your strongest and be ready to prove it.

 - Credibility marketing to developers: you understand why gated whitepapers fail with this audience and what works instead.

 - A track record of experiments that changed a number, with the honesty to tell us which ones failed.

 - Analytics fluency: you can build your own reporting, and you know the difference between a lift and a coincidence.

 - Comfort in the build layer. You can ship a landing page yourself, read the console, and work in whatever the site is built on rather than waiting on engineering.

 - A proven AI builder mindset: you've shipped automations and creative pipelines using LLMs, not just used ChatGPT.


NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a PLG or self-serve developer product with a free tier.

 - SQL and comfort querying a warehouse directly.

 - Experience with developer-native paid channels and sponsorship buying.

 - Hands-on with the modern web stack (Next.js, Webflow, or similar) and CRO tooling.

 - Early experience with AI answer visibility and how it differs from classic SEO.
   
   


BENEFITS

 - Health and wellness: Premium medical, dental, and vision coverage, plus a monthly wellness benefit and a monthly commuter benefit for our SF team.

 - Fertility and family planning: Reimbursement for eligible egg freezing and related medical expenses up to a $15,000 lifetime maximum, plus 16 weeks of fully paid parental leave for all new parents, whether through birth, adoption, surrogacy, or foster placement.

 - Life at Exa: Lunch and dinner served daily, an office stocked with snacks, coffee, and health supplements, fresh bread from a local bakery every morning, weekly milk tea deliveries, monthly picnics, and parties to celebrate the wins (and each other).

 - Visa sponsorship: We sponsor visas for exceptional candidates and welcome applicants from all backgrounds and locations.

Exa is an equal opportunity employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regard to race, creed, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity or expression, national origin, disability, age, veteran status, marital status, pregnancy or related conditions, criminal histories consistent with applicable law, or any other basis protected by applicable law.

Read more https://exa.ai/blog/announcing-series-c

We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We’re high agency, low-ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We're scaling in Singapore and need someone on the ground who owns the people and workplace side of things. You'd be the first dedicated ops person in our Singapore office, which means you'll shape how we grow from 5 people to 10, 20, and beyond.🚀 

This role sits between our People lead in San Francisco and your team in Singapore. You're the point person making sure everyone has what they need to do their best work - from handling the day-to-day office logistics to making sure new hires feel genuinely welcomed, to keeping our employment and benefits operations clean and compliant across the region.

We’re looking for someone who will care deeply about making people's experience at Exa feel good, whether that's a smooth first day or knowing exactly who to talk to when they have a question. You'll also be the one keeping the gears turning behind the scenes - the office runs, the visas process smoothly, the vendors get paid on time.




WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Run onboarding for every new Singapore hire - from offer to first day - and make it feel like a warm welcome

 - Help people relocating to Singapore get oriented on the ground - housing, neighborhoods, what they need to know about living and working here

 - Coordinate with our global payroll provider and employment counsel to make sure work permits move smoothly

 - Own benefits administration for the Singapore team, including health insurance coordination and answering employee questions

 - Manage office logistics and facilities as we expand

 - Keep our people data accurate and organized

 - Support our accounting and compliance partners to make sure expense management is clean and accurate

 - Be the friendly first point of contact for employees with questions about benefits, visas, office logistics, or anything else

 - Build the runbooks and systems that let us scale without chaos

 - Help with company events, offsites, and team moments that people actually look forward to

 - Constantly look for ways to improve the employee experience - from small details to bigger operational improvements
   
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 3-5 years of experience in people ops, HR, office management, or startup operations

 - Familiarity with Singapore employment practices and MOM requirements

 - Exceptional organization - you manage multiple vendors, timelines, and details without dropping things

 - Strong written communication and the ability to be a warm, reliable point of contact for employees

 - Discretion with sensitive information and good judgment about what actually matters

 - A bias toward action - you figure things out independently, especially in a fast-growing environment

 - Strong ownership mentality - you don't wait to be asked to fix problems

 - Genuine care for the people you support, and a real interest in making Exa a place people love working at
   
   


BONUS

 - Experience at a top-tier startup or scale-up

 - You've helped scale a company through rapid growth

 - Experience coordinating across multiple countries or time zones




WHY THIS ROLE MATTERS

A company is only as good as the people in it, and the systems that support them. We're building something extraordinary in Singapore, and we need someone who cares about getting both right - making sure our team feels supported and that the operational infrastructure keeps pace with our growth. If that's the kind of work you want to do, we'd love to meet you.



This is an in-person opportunity in Singapore.

The Head of Marketing Operations builds the infrastructure that lets Exa marketing scale, and runs the operating system that keeps the team performing day to day. You will own the marketing tech stack, the data model, the lifecycle, and the analytics that turn marketing into a predictable pipeline engine the executive team can trust.

jobs.title: Growth Marketing Manger
jobs.description:
ABOUT EXA

We raised a $250M Series C to build the search engine for AIs. Led by a16z, with existing investors Benchmark, Lightspeed, and YC doubling down, the round brings Exa's valuation to $2.2 billion.

Exa is building a search engine for the AI era. Our Search API currently powers agents, Fortune 500s, and AI labs as we transform an industry that hasn't been disrupted since the 90s. We're a largely SF-based team of ~100 from Harvard, MIT, Meta, Google Research, ex-founders, and dropouts alike.

We are rapidly building the most intelligent search engine in history. We're high agency, low ego, and united by the feeling that this is one of the last problems worth getting right.

We are looking for a Lifecycle Marketing Manager to build the programs that turn new developer signups into activated users and engaged enterprise opportunities.




ABOUT THE ROLE

We have two lifecycle motions moving at completely different speeds. A developer signs up, and within minutes either makes a successful API call or drifts away. An enterprise account can take months to move, involve a dozen people, and require sustained education across technical and business stakeholders. You own both as deliberately separate tracks.

On the self-serve side, the work is activation: getting a new signup to their first successful API call, then building the habits and usage signals that indicate real intent. The best programs will feel more like useful product guidance than marketing. Anything generic will be ignored.

On the enterprise side, you build the journeys that keep Exa credible through a long buying cycle: persona-based education, buying committee engagement, stalled opportunity reactivation, and the content paths that help an account move from interest to evaluation.

You will also own the lifecycle side of our webinar program: audience strategy, promotion, segmentation, and follow-up. PMM, DevRel, founders, and other subject matter experts will shape the topic and host. You will make sure the right people attend and that interest turns into meaningful next steps.

This is an AI-first role at an AI-first company. Personalization, drafting, journey QA, segmentation, and reporting should be AI-accelerated so one person can operate two strong lifecycle motions without creating a pile of manual work.

This role is based in person at our San Francisco HQ.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN




SELF-SERVE ACTIVATION

 - Own the developer journey from signup to first successful API call, early repeat usage, and an agreed activation or PQL threshold.

 - Build product-triggered messaging, onboarding sequences, and interventions that recover stalled new users.

 - Partner closely with Product and Engineering on the broader onboarding experience while owning the lifecycle programs that support it.

 - Success is measured by signup-to-first-call conversion, early repeat usage, and the percentage of new users who reach activation or PQL thresholds.




ENTERPRISE NURTURE

 - Own the long-cycle journeys for enterprise accounts.

 - Build education paths by persona, use case, and vertical.

 - Develop programs that engage the broader buying committee, support active evaluations, and bring dormant accounts or opportunities back into motion.

 - Success is measured by meaningful account engagement, buying committee coverage, dormant opportunities reactivated, and progression into qualified pipeline.




LIFECYCLE SEGMENTATION AND ORCHESTRATION

 - Own who receives what, when, and why.

 - Build a clear segmentation strategy across developers, product-qualified accounts, enterprise buyers, active evaluations, and dormant prospects.

 - Use product behavior, account context, and buying stage to determine the right message and next step.

 - Own send governance so no one receives conflicting, repetitive, or irrelevant communication from Exa.




EMAIL CRAFT AND PROGRAM QUALITY

 - Own what we send and how it reads.

 - Set the quality bar for lifecycle copy, subject lines, cadence, personalization, and calls to action.

 - Make sure every message earns the attention it asks for, especially when the audience is a developer.

 - Success is measured by program-level engagement, conversion, unsubscribe rates, and the absence of internal collisions.




WEBINAR AUDIENCE AND CONVERSION

 - Own audience strategy, promotion, segmentation, and follow-up for webinars and virtual programs.

 - Partner with PMM, DevRel, founders, and other subject matter experts on topics and speakers.

 - Make sure the right accounts register, attend, and move into an appropriate next step after the event.

 - Success is measured by qualified attendance, target-account participation, meetings created, and post-event pipeline progression.




EXPERIMENTATION AND REPORTING

 - Own the lifecycle testing roadmap and performance reporting.

 - Build a disciplined backlog of experiments across activation, timing, segmentation, messaging, and re-engagement.

 - Be clear about what was tested, what happened, and what changed as a result.

 - Marketing Operations owns the attribution model and source of truth. You own lifecycle performance within it and use the same numbers as the rest of the company.




AI-FIRST EXECUTION

 - Design AI-powered workflows for drafting, personalization, audience research, journey QA, segmentation, and performance summaries.

 - Use AI to increase the quality and speed of the work, not to flood inboxes with more content.

 - If a step runs manually more than twice, you should be itching to automate it.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - New developer signups reach their first successful API call at a materially higher rate than they do today.

 - More new users reach repeat usage and product-qualified thresholds.

 - Enterprise accounts stay engaged through long buying cycles without being spammed.

 - Dormant accounts and opportunities are brought back into active conversations.

 - The self-serve and enterprise motions are genuinely distinct in content, cadence, audience, and tone.

 - Lifecycle segmentation reflects product behavior, account context, and buying stage.

 - Webinars consistently attract people from the accounts we care about and produce meaningful follow-up.

 - Every send has a clear purpose, and stale programs get retired rather than accumulating.

 - Lifecycle performance is visible, trusted, and reviewed regularly with Marketing, Product, Sales, and Marketing Operations.




WHAT THIS ROLE DOES NOT OWN

 - Post-sale onboarding, customer adoption, and expansion: Customer Success, Product, and Account Management own the customer lifecycle after purchase. This role may support relevant communications but is not the primary owner.

 - Marketing automation platform, data model, deliverability infrastructure, lead scoring, and attribution: Marketing Operations owns the plumbing. You own the programs built on top of it.

 - Paid channels, website, and landing page infrastructure: Digital Marketing.

 - Technical content substance, benchmarks, and organic discovery: Technical PMM for Content.

 - In-product onboarding UI and product experiences: Product and Engineering. You will partner closely with them.

 - Webinar production logistics and speaker content: PMM, DevRel, and the relevant subject matter experts. You own audience strategy, promotion, and follow-up.

 - Field events and regional programs: Field Marketing and Field Events.

 - Sales sequences and outbound prospecting cadences: Sales and RevOps.




WHO YOU ARE

 - 5+ years in lifecycle, growth, email, or marketing automation at a B2B technology company, with hands-on ownership of programs you built and measured yourself.

 - Experience building both a self-serve product-led motion and an enterprise nurture motion, with a clear understanding of why they require different approaches.

 - Deep craft in email. Show us sequences you wrote and be ready to explain the reasoning behind the audience, subject line, length, cadence, and call to action.

 - Experience using product behavior and account signals to trigger and personalize lifecycle programs.

 - Credibility with a developer audience. You understand why most marketing email fails with engineers and can write something they will actually read.

 - A track record of improving activation, engagement, pipeline progression, or reactivation through programs you personally owned.

 - Experience supporting webinars or virtual programs through audience strategy, promotion, segmentation, and post-event conversion.

 - Experimentation discipline. You have run real tests, written honest readouts, and changed programs based on what the results showed.

 - Analytics fluency. You can build your own reporting, investigate performance, and tell the difference between a lift and a coincidence.

 - Working knowledge of deliverability fundamentals, consent, preference management, and list hygiene, enough to partner well with Marketing Operations.

jobs.description:

We are looking for a Head of Marketing, APJ based in Sydney to lead Exa's marketing across Asia Pacific and Japan.




ABOUT THE ROLE

This is Exa's first senior marketing leader outside the United States. You will set the marketing strategy for Asia Pacific and Japan and run it as a commercial function, tied to the region's pipeline number. APJ is many markets with different buyers, languages, and routes to market. Deciding which ones matter first, and how Exa wins in each, is the core of the job.

Sales coverage is coming online across ANZ, Southeast Asia, and India, with a partner-led motion in Japan. You will be the marketing counterpart: deciding where to invest, which motions to run in which markets, and how a fast-moving American AI infrastructure company earns credibility with buyers in Sydney, Tokyo, Singapore, and Bengaluru.

This is a player-coach role. You will write the regional plan and then help execute it yourself, from shaping a campaign and adapting the message to hosting an executive dinner and sitting in pipeline reviews with Sales. You start as a team of one, with meaningful budget for field events, conferences, and developer events. We expect your first hire, an early-career field events marketer, to join within months, with more headcount as growth justifies.

Exa's buyers are technical, and much of our growth starts with developers who sign up and build before anyone talks to Sales. The right person understands both product-led growth with developers and account-based programs for enterprise buyers. You will work closely with Sales, Product, and Marketing to keep all of it pointed at the same priorities.

This is an AI-first role at an AI-first company. Account research, localization, campaign analysis, and reporting should be workflows you build, since one person covering a dozen markets only works if the work is automated.

This role is based in-person in Sydney, with regular travel across APJ and periodic trips to our San Francisco HQ.




WHAT YOU'LL OWN




APJ MARKETING STRATEGY

Own the regional marketing plan. Translate Exa's global priorities into a plan for APJ, prioritize markets by opportunity and sales coverage, and decide where to invest across markets and programs. Own the APJ marketing budget, which centers on field events, conferences, developer events, and selective local sponsorships (including developer creators and communities). Success is measured by revenue growth.




GO-TO-MARKET BY MARKET

Build a go-to-market approach for priority markets across ANZ, Japan, Southeast Asia, and India. The right motion differs by market (direct, partner-led, or channel-based), and some markets should wait until product-led signal justifies the spend.




PIPELINE AND DEMAND

Own APJ pipeline targets. Build the programs that create qualified opportunities and move them through the cycle: account-based campaigns, executive dinners, a small number of high-value trade shows, reactivation of any stalled pipeline, and webinars or localized content. Use pipeline and conversion data to shift investment toward what works. Success is measured by pipeline and by cost per opportunity.




SALES PARTNERSHIP

Be the marketing partner to APJ Sales, SDRs, and regional partners. Align on ICP, target accounts, campaign priorities, lead routing, and follow-up, and run a regular operating rhythm. Success is measured by lead-to-opportunity conversion and by seller satisfaction with campaigns and enablement.




PLG IN REGION

Ensure APJ developers and AI-native companies find Exa, sign up, and build. Run developer events, hackathons, and meetups in the region with DevRel support, sponsor local developer creators and communities where they reach the right builders, and work with Digital and Growth Marketing on inbound quality and conversion. Use sign-up and usage signal to tell Sales where to engage. Success is measured by sign-ups and PQL-sourced pipeline.




EXA STORY IN APJ

Adapt Exa's global positioning for APJ buyers, identifying where the story needs local proof, language, or emphasis. Bring customer and market insight into messaging, launches, and the roadmap through Product Marketing. Keep brand and demand working as one program. Success is measured by regional launch success.




AGENCIES, PARTNERS, AND VENDORS

Select and manage agencies, event vendors, and marketing partners across the region, including co-marketing with channel and cloud partners. Make sure each one understands the priorities, and delivers quality work.




TEAM BUILDING

Hire and lead the APJ marketing team as the region grows, starting with an field events manager. Set the bar, develop people, and build a function that executes without you in every room.




WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

 - APJ has a marketing plan with clear market priorities, tied to the regional pipeline number, and Sales co-owns it.

 - Marketing-sourced and influenced pipeline in APJ is measured, growing, and trusted by Sales and Finance.

 - Each priority market has a working motion (direct, partner-led, or product-led) chosen on evidence.

 - APJ developers and AI-native companies adopt Exa at a rate that feeds Sales.

 - Exa has credible local customer stories in ANZ, Japan, and at least one other market.

 - Investment shifts quarter to quarter based on what the data says.

 - Your first hire is in seat and performing, and the playbook you built makes each new market faster to open.




YOU SHOULD HAVE

 - 10+ years in B2B marketing at technology companies, including 3+ years leading marketing for APJ or a major part of it (ANZ plus at least one Asian market).

 - A record of owning a regional pipeline number and budget, and of deciding where to invest across markets. You can reconstruct the numbers live.

 - Hands-on experience with both direct and partner-led go-to-market, ideally including Japan.

 - Strong sales partnership: an operating rhythm you built with Sales and SDRs, and an example of pushing back on a seller request you thought was wrong.

 - Deep field and event craft. You have run conferences, executive dinners, and developer events yourself, and can still build and run a campaign end to end.

 - Comfort with a technical product and technical buyers. You can hold a real conversation about APIs, agents, and retrieval.

 - Experience building a region for a US-headquartered company, operating semi-autonomously across time zones.

 - Evidence you have hired and developed marketers.

 - A proven AI builder mindset. You have shipped automations or internal tools with LLMs and can show us.




NICE TO HAVE

 - Experience at a developer tools, API-first, cloud, or data infrastructure company.

 - Experience running product-led growth alongside an enterprise sales motion.

 - Japanese, Mandarin, or another regional language.

 - Relationships with regional cloud providers, systems integrators, or developer communities.

 - Experience launching a region from zero at an early-stage company.
